title: Without Replacement Changed The Second Denominator And Numerator
text: id: COMP-006 domain: math title: Without Replacement Changed The Second Denominator And Numerator tags: probability, without-replacement, fractions memory: I once missed a probability because I kept the bag unchanged after the first draw. Without replacement meant the second red count dropped and the total count dropped. The multiplication became first chance times changed second chance. After simplifying the fraction, I wrote a decimal or percent so the size of the chance was visible. The fraction looked ordinary, but the changed denominator carried the whole meaning.

title: Fractions Simplified After The Correct Multiplication
text: id: COMP-020 domain: math title: Fractions Simplified After The Correct Multiplication tags: fractions, probability, simplify memory: A probability fraction once simplified beautifully from the wrong multiplication. I learned to get the event structure correct before reducing anything. First the changed counts, then multiplication, then simplification, then an optional decimal. A neat fraction is only useful after the setup is true.
